records.title: Dual-Targeted Hybrid Exosome-Liposome Nanoparticles Potentiate Antitumor Efficacy and Promote Immune Infiltration in Ovarian Cancer.
records.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is the most lethal gynecological malignancy within female reproductive system malignancies. Chemoresistance and metastasis are major challenges for OC treatment, highlighting the urgent necessity for novel therapeutic strategies. Doxorubicin (Dox) is frequently adopted in OC treatment, owing to its minimal peripheral neurotoxicity, negligible glycemic fluctuation impact, and favorable combined therapeutic efficacy with platinum. However, its clinical application is largely limited, especially by profound cardiotoxicity, rapid clearance, and drug resistance. We engineered Epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) and folate receptor alpha (FRα) dual-targeted hybrid exosome-liposome nanoparticles (siUSP43/Dox@DT-HENPs) by integrating the high drug-loading capacity of liposomes with the MPS-evasive property of CD47-overexpressing exosomes. Comprehensive validation in cell lines, animal models, and patient-derived organoids (PDOs) confirmed their targeting specificity and therapeutic efficacy. As expected, siUSP43/Dox@DT-HENPs successfully achieved precise delivery of Dox, reduced mononuclear phagocyte clearance, minimized immune cytotoxicity, and enhanced immune infiltration, highlighting their promising potential in OC treatment.

records.title: Human retinal organoid integration into 3D neural tissue models - an emerging opportunity.
records.abstract: Human retinal and brain organoids are transforming research into human neural development, disease and regenerative medicine, reproducing key structural, molecular and functional features of the retina and brain and providing an experimentally accessible model. However, these systems have largely been developed in isolation, limiting their ability to model the long-range neuronal connectivity that underlies visual function and the shared mechanisms of retinal and central nervous system disease. Recent advances in assembloid technologies, tissue engineering and computational analysis now make the generation of integrated human eye-brain models an increasingly realistic goal. In this review, we focus on the integration of retinal and brain organoids to reconstruct elements of the human visual pathway. We discuss advances in retinal and brain organoid differentiation that improve maturation, reproducibility and physiological fidelity, including vascularization, glial incorporation, extracellular matrix engineering and functional electrophysiological assessment. We examine strategies for assembling multi-regional neural tissues to promote retinal ganglion cell projection, target-specific connectivity and circuit formation and consider how eye-brain assembloids could provide platforms to investigate retinal and neurological disorders while accelerating therapeutic discovery and human tissue-based preclinical testing. Finally, we discuss the technical and biological challenges that remain, including incomplete maturation, standardisation, scalability and functional validation, and highlight how advances are likely to drive the next generation of physiologically relevant human visual system models. By integrating developments across retinal organoids, brain organoids and assembloid technologies, this review outlines a framework for modelling human eye-brain connectivity and defines the opportunities and challenges that will shape this emerging field.

records.title: Targeting PLAUR restores paclitaxel sensitivity in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma by suppressing NF-κB signaling.
records.abstract: Paclitaxel is a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), yet its clinical efficacy is frequently compromised by drug resistance. To address this challenge, we performed an unbiased screening approach to identify resistance-associated molecular targets with therapeutic potential. PLAUR expression was systematically analyzed in paclitaxel-resistant ESCC cell lines, clinical ESCC specimens, and public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. Genetic loss- and gain-of-function approaches were employed to evaluate the impact of PLAUR on paclitaxel sensitivity and apoptosis in ESCC cells. NF-κB pathway activation was assessed by transcriptomic profiling and western blot analysis. The effects of PLAUR depletion and cenupatide (UPARANT) treatment were evaluated in patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and xenograft models. PLAUR was consistently upregulated in paclitaxel-resistant ESCC cells, tumor tissues from poor responders, and malignant epithelial cell clusters associated with poor therapeutic response identified by single-cell analysis. Genetic ablation of PLAUR significantly enhanced paclitaxel-induced apoptosis and reduced drug resistance, whereas PLAUR re-expression conferred resistance. Mechanistically, PLAUR promoted paclitaxel resistance by activating the NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby suppressing apoptosis. Inhibition of NF-κB signaling attenuated PLAUR-associated resistance. Cenupatide enhanced paclitaxel sensitivity in the tested cell, PDO, and xenograft models. PLAUR contributes to paclitaxel resistance in ESCC through NF-κB-associated suppression of apoptosis. These preclinical findings support further evaluation of cenupatide-mediated paclitaxel sensitization in ESCC.

records.title: P300 as an epigenetic regulatory node linking berberine to attenuated H3K27ac/STAT3 inflammatory transcription in ulcerative colitis.
records.abstract: Berberine (BBR) attenuates experimental colitis, but its effects on colonic p300-associated signaling remain unclear. We used network pharmacology and two-sample Mendelian randomization to prioritize BBR-associated genes on the basis of genetically predicted blood gene expression and ulcerative colitis (UC) risk. These analyses identified EP300 as a candidate. In UC-derived organoids, regions with greater accessibility in cultures from previously inflamed mucosa were overrepresented in the highest EP300 signal bin of an independent sigmoid-colon ChIP-seq dataset. Predicted STAT3 motifs were more frequent in regions with higher reference EP300 signal. The predicted BBR pose in the p300 acetyltransferase domain overlapped the crystallographic acetyl-CoA site. In mice with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis, BBR reduced disease activity, histological injury and mucosal cytokine levels and increased colonic ZO-1 and occludin staining. Colonic p300 abundance, H3K27ac staining, STAT3 phosphorylation and Il17a mRNA were lower with BBR than with DSS alone. C646 alone also reduced disease activity, histological injury and colonic Stat3 and Il17a mRNA. Compared with BBR alone, BBR + C646 further reduced H3K27ac staining, STAT3 phosphorylation and Il17a mRNA, whereas BBR + TTK21 partially reversed these changes. These results support a contribution of p300-associated regulation to the response to BBR in experimental colitis.

records.title: Mapping the Developmental Landscape of Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes and Cardiac Organoids Relative to Native Heart Tissue.
records.abstract: The development of physiologically relevant human cardiac models is essential for drug discovery and disease modeling; however, achieving the transcriptomic and metabolic maturity of adult human tissue remains a challenge. In this study, we performed a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic comparison of in vitro-induced pluripotent stem cell cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) in 2D cultures, 3D cardiac organoids, and native fetal and adult human cardiac tissue. CMs from both 2D and organoid cultures were immature compared to adult CMs. 3D organoids exhibit a more complex cellular architecture comprising multiple cardiac cell types, and they possess a unique proliferative fibroblast population that is not represented in the adult or fetal heart. Organoids also showed immaturity in non-CMs as well as CM cell types. Both iPSC-CMs and cardiac organoids were metabolically immature with enhanced expression of both glycolytic and reduced fatty acid oxidation genes. However, maturation was not a binary state, as the in vitro CMs were distinct from fetal CMs, and had transcriptionally advanced calcium handling and electrophysiology, but immature metabolism and stress responses. When assessed versus adult heart tissues they were also distinct. Our work provides a molecular roadmap of the gaps between in vitro models and the native adult heart, highlighting areas for future improvement in in vitro CMs.

records.title: The Tumor Microenvironment in Esophageal Adenocarcinoma: From Cellular Ecosystems to Therapy-Driven Dynamics.
records.abstract: Esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) is among the most aggressive tumors for incidence and mortality worldwide. In recent years, the composition and spatial architecture of the tumor microenvironment (TME) have emerged as critical determinants of tumor biology, therapeutic response, and prognosis. In EAC, the limited efficacy of approved conventional therapies boosted the study of molecular and cellular determinants of response within the TME. In this review, we provide an overview of the major cellular components of EAC TME, highlighting their functional interactions within the tumor ecosystem. We further dissect the bidirectional interplay between TME cells and therapeutic strategies. Interestingly, the increasing understanding of TME dynamics opens new avenues in cancer therapies, supporting the development and clinical investigation of TME-targeted approaches. The complexity of TME ecosystem has also accelerated the implementation of advanced methods for high-resolution molecular and structural characterization. Spatial multi-OMICs technologies and advanced patient-derived organoids (PDOs) models demonstrated their strength in dissecting TME biology and modeling clinically relevant therapeutic response. Overall, these integrative methodologies are redefining the understanding of EAC TME biology, bolstering the development of functionally informed models capable of facilitating patients' stratification and personalized therapeutic strategies.

records.title: A Testable Framework for Mechanics-Conditioned Perturbation Models in Drug Discovery.
records.abstract: Perturbation-predictive cell models are advancing quickly, yet they remain predominantly molecular, even though the mechanical state of cells and tissues-stiffness, viscoelasticity, geometry, and force generation-can alter therapeutic response. This review converts that observation into a testable program. It separates four claims that are routinely conflated and gives each its own baseline, estimand, design, and named refutation condition: whether auxiliary mechanical measurements improve prediction of treatment response beyond a complete non-mechanical baseline (H1); whether mechanics computed from images help as a representation rather than as added information (H2); whether experimentally controlled mechanical context modifies treatment effects, including once local drug exposure is held comparable (H3 and H3a); and whether mechanics-aware predictions improve preclinical prioritization decisions under a fixed budget (H4). Current evidence is graded against an explicit, reproducible rubric, and the two links the framework actually requires, mechanical conditioning of perturbation response and prospectively validated mechanics-aware decisions, are unpopulated. A worked pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma program specifies donors, materials, gemcitabine exposure measurement, endpoints, simulation-based power, staged costs, and a blinded decision test, with a reduced-scope minimum implementation for groups that cannot execute the full design. The practical contribution for a bioengineering readership is a transferable specification checklist, covering measurement provenance, units of assignment and inference, leakage control, effect margins, and decision rules, to be completed before resources are committed. We conclude that mechanics should enter perturbation models as a hypothesis carrying a refutation condition, not as a default enrichment. Explicit limitations bound the work: the synthesis is targeted rather than systematic, the evidence grades were assigned by a single assessor, and the framework has not itself been executed.

records.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: Current Evidence, Multiscale Modeling Approaches, and Challenges in Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
records.abstract: Digital Twin (DT), a dynamic simulation technology derived from the engineering field, has been deeply integrated into the field of tumor precision medicine, empowered by both multi-omics technologies and artificial intelligence. It offers a novel approach to overcoming the limitations of traditional paradigms in tumor research, diagnosis, and treatment. This article reviews the full-scale application system of tumor DT, spanning from the molecular to the individual level, and constructs a progressive simulation architecture of "virtual cell-virtual knockout/virtual overexpression-virtual organoid-virtual patient". The virtual cell enables the in silico representation of tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment, serving as the fundamental unit for dissecting molecular mechanisms. Virtual knockout/overexpression provides non-invasive, high-throughput methods for target prioritization, significantly shortening research and development cycles. The virtual organoid achieves computational reconstruction of the three-dimensional (3D) tumor microenvironment, bridging the gap between single-cell and individual-scale simulations. The virtual patient, in turn, supports personalized therapeutic decision-making and virtual clinical trials. By synthesizing the latest research findings in the field, this article delineates the technical pathways, primary modeling tools, and representative empirical cases for each application tier. It further provides an in-depth analysis of core challenges, including multi-source data heterogeneity, insufficient model accuracy and interpretability, and obstacles to clinical translation. Corresponding solutions, such as data standardization, cross-scale technology integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration between medicine and engineering, are proposed. The aim is to provide a comprehensive reference for leveraging DT to advance tumor research and facilitate its translation into clinical practice.

records.title: SparseKG-Flow: A Virtual Cell Generative Architecture Unifying Structural Causal Models and Knowledge Graph Priors for Single-Cell Drug Perturbation Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting single-cell responses to new drugs is essential for mechanism-aware virtual cell modeling, yet existing models often fail on unseen drugs or cell types by relying on memorized correlations rather than transferable mechanisms. SparseKG-Flow addresses this out-of-distribution (OOD) challenge as a generative architecture integrating three inductive biases: a sparse drug-effect encoder with Gumbel-Softmax gating, a heterogeneous graph adapter for drug-target-pathway knowledge, and a mechanism-guided residual flow decoder. On Tahoe-100M, it achieves Pearson r of 0.942 and 0.920 under Test-NewDrug and Test-NewCell settings, respectively, outperforming the next-best baseline by 16.6% and 14.8%. It also reduces Δ expression error by 89.0% and 91.7%, respectively, and more than doubles held-out-drug top-gene recovery (Overlap@50 = 0.210). Frozen-model evaluation on high-grade serous ovarian cancer patient data provides preliminary evidence of transfer beyond the Tahoe-100M panel. Ablations confirm all components aid OOD generalization, with the molecular knowledge adapter contributing the most. SparseKG-Flow further reorganizes pharmacological priors into interpretable, task-trained representations and highlights Abemaciclib, Capmatinib, and Gemcitabine in A549 analysis. It thus serves as both an accurate perturbation predictor and a mechanism-grounded virtual cell platform for therapeutic prioritization.

records.title: MitoLODE: a virtual mitochondrion framework with knowledge graph priors for trajectory modeling and mechanistic perturbation analysis.
records.abstract: Mitochondria play a central role in the pathogenesis of major diseases. Tracking how they evolve under disease conditions is valuable for understanding pathological mechanisms and identifying intervention windows. Existing single-cell trajectory inference methods rely on pseudotime rather than a real temporal axis, and rarely model disease and control as independent trajectories. Virtual cell methods target one-shot drug perturbation responses and do not handle the continuous temporal evolution of disease phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose a virtual mitochondrion research paradigm. We first curate and construct MitoKG, a mitochondria-specific heterogeneous knowledge graph integrated from five authoritative databases. MitoKG contains 2549 nodes of four types and 23 019 edges of five relation types. Building on these priors, we develop MitoLODE, a conditioned dual-trajectory neural ordinary differential equation framework. MitoLODE embeds graph priors and temporal features throughout encoding, continuous-time dynamics, and decoding, modeling disease and control evolution as two coupled paths. Benchmarked against eight baselines across four datasets covering Parkinson's disease, cardiac, and pancreatic differentiation, MitoLODE leads in most settings and remains robust under low-data regimes and extrapolation to unseen time points. Two synthetic datasets with known ground truth validate its trajectory recovery under controlled conditions. Building on the trained model, we design a gradient-guided perturbation procedure that identifies potential intervention targets aligned with known Parkinson's pathology. We develop MGMI, a large language model-based reasoning module that grounds model outputs in MitoKG nodes and turns them into confidence-graded mechanistic hypotheses, which nonetheless require experimental validation.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: EvoSeq: A Eukaryotic Sequence-Function Profiling Platform for AI-Guided Engineering of Genome-Editing Enzymes.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping protein engineering, yet progress remains constrained by the limited availability of scalable, normalized sequence-activity datasets and experimental benchmarks. Reported here is Evolution by Sequencing (EvoSeq), a sequencing-based profiling platform for genome-editing enzymes that links each variant to a reporter sequence change, enabling activity and variant sequence to be quantified together by next-generation sequencing. Representative sequencing-assisted workflows either require separate functional assays or were performed in bacteria. EvoSeq performs sequence-activity profiling in eukaryotic yeast system with reduced background by up to 95-fold compared to bacterial system, positioning EvoSeq as a pooled eukaryotic alternative to workflows that require separate functional assays and to approaches demonstrated primarily in bacteria. Application to adenine base editor evolution identifies variants with 1.4-fold higher on-target activity at a HBG gene target and threefold lower off-target editing at PCSK9 after mRNA-lipid nanoparticle validation in HepG2 cells. An intron-embedded homologous-recombination recording strategy further enables direct evolution of the large Cas12i nuclease CasY7 and supports active learning, increasing the hit rate of model-nominated mutational windows compared with manual selection. EvoSeq therefore provides an experimental benchmarking method for AI-guided protein-design algorithms and AI-compatible sequence-activity profiling platform for engineering genome editors in eukaryotic cells.

records.title: [Advances in ProteinMPNN-driven protein engineering].
records.abstract: Biomanufacturing is a key pathway for promoting the green transformation of conventional production methods. Its core bottleneck lies in the difficulty of natural enzymes to meet the requirements of industrial applications, necessitating the customized modification of enzyme molecules through protein engineering. Conventional semi-rational design is limited by a narrow sequence search space, heavy reliance on known structural information, and high experimental screening costs, which make it difficult to achieve precise design of industrial-grade enzyme molecules. In recent years, artificial intelligence-based protein design technologies represented by ProteinMPNN have made breakthrough progress and are driving a profound paradigm shift in protein engineering. This article systematically describes the technical principles, workflow, and methodological advantages of ProteinMPNN, compares it with Rosetta and other protein design models, and reviews the research progress of this technology in industrial enzyme engineering and biomanufacturing. On this basis, this article discusses current research hotspots and challenges in industrial application, and provides an outlook on future development directions and prospects for industrial implementation. It is expected to serve as a reference for fundamental research and industrial translation in synthetic biology and protein engineering.

records.title: Modeling Protein Evolution with Generative Models: From Extant Sequence Data to Evolutionary Dynamics.
records.abstract: Protein sequences carry a record of evolutionary history shaped by mutation, selection, drift, and epistasis. Recent generative models trained on homologous sequence families offer a new way to read this record: they define probabilistic landscapes that score sequences, generate viable variants, and capture constraints that are difficult to measure experimentally. In this review, we discuss how such landscapes can be used not only for protein design or mutation-effect prediction, but also for modeling evolutionary dynamics. We focus particularly on Direct Coupling Analysis as an interpretable and experimentally validated framework, while placing it in the broader context of generative sequence modeling. We first describe how generative sequence landscapes are inferred and assessed, then review how they can be coupled to population-genetic or substitution-model dynamics to simulate protein evolution across experimental and phylogenetic timescales. Applications include viral evolution, laboratory drift experiments, historical contingency, entrenchment, epistatic drift over time, and long-term sequence-space exploration. We conclude by discussing open challenges, including score-fitness calibration, phylogenetic structure, codon-level mutation biases, indels, and the integration of experimental data.

records.title: ATC Classification and Scaffold-Split pMIC Prediction for Antibacterial Prioritization.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance requires reproducible computational tools that distinguish antibacterial-drug class membership from measured antibacterial potency. We developed a descriptor-based workflow for Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification (ATC)-based prioritization, exploratory molecular generation, and pMIC prediction. ChEMBL 33 structures were encoded using Mordred descriptors. Fourteen classifiers were used to distinguish 248 systemic antibacterial drugs (ATC J01/J04A) from 2540 non-anti-infective reference drugs. Models were assessed by random, independent, and Bemis-Murcko scaffold splits; An exploratory character-level recurrent neural network was used for molecular generation. Separately, eight regressors modeled Staphylococcus aureus pMIC for 33,505 compounds under a scaffold split. Random forest achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.857 on the random-split test set and 0.775 on the independent validation set. For unseen scaffolds, the MCC was 0.746; after removal of six β-lactam ring descriptors, the MCC was 0.738. Across 25 repeated scaffold splits, the random forest test MCC was 0.774 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.752-0.795), supporting the consistency of scaffold-based performance across partitions. Char-RNN validity was 10.8%; the generated molecules were novel relative to the training set (23/25 were also absent from ChEMBL) and synthesizable. Novelty is reported relative to the training set rather than as absolute chemical-space novelty. XGBoost achieved a scaffold-held-out pMIC R2 = 0.510, RMSE = 0.743 log units, and a Spearman ρ = 0.695. Across 10 repeated scaffold splits, XGBoost R2 was 0.505 (95% CI 0.472-0.537), matching the single-split value. On two independent external tests-a 2019-2022 temporal split and 5090 compounds new in the later ChEMBL 37 release - absolute accuracy was lower (R2 = 0.240 and 0.286) while rank correlation was retained (Spearman ρ = 0.502 and 0.566). These results are consistent with the model being prioritized rather than being used for accurate potency-prediction. The ATC classifier prioritizes structures resembling approved antibacterial drugs rather than establishing measured antibacterial activity. The pMIC model provides scaffold-aware estimates of S. aureus potency; both components require assessment of the applicability domain and experimental validation.

records.title: Design of High-Affinity Mini-Protein Drug Conjugates Targeting TROP2.
records.abstract: Accurate and effective treatment of solid tumors has long been a core issue in cancer therapy. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a crucial breakthrough in precision oncology. Traditional ADCs rely on monoclonal antibodies generated through animal immunization, followed by screening, sequencing, and recombinant expressiona process that is experimentally complex and costly. In this study, we employed deep learning-based computational design methods to design mini-protein binders targeting the tumor-associated antigen TROP2. The designed TROP2 mini-protein binder exhibited high specificity and thermal stability. The binding affinity was optimized from 40.4 nM to 628 pM through partial diffusion. On this basis, we engineered the mini-protein binder by conjugating it with the microtubule inhibitor VcMMAE, thereby constructing mini-protein drug conjugates (MPDCs) that can specifically target and kill TROP2-positive tumor cells. A comprehensive assessment of the anti-tumor efficacy of these MPDCs was performed using cancer cell lines, organoid models, and mouse xenograft models.

records.title: Borophene-Gold Nanohybrid Immunosensor for In Situ EV Lysis and Cancer Biomarker Detection by Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived biomarkers provide valuable molecular information for early cancer detection and disease monitoring, yet their analysis typically requires labor-intensive EV isolation and chemical lysis, limiting access and increasing assay complexity. Here, we present a label-free, non-faradaic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (nf-EIS) biosensor based on liquid-phase-exfoliated borophene (BP) integrated onto gold electrodes for direct detection of circulating and EV-derived biomarkers in serum. BP-Au interface provides an electrochemically active, high-capacitance sensing surface via interfacial charge transfer and orbital interactions, while electron-deficient boron sites enable direct coordination with glutaraldehyde and stable antibody immobilization without insulating linker layers. To improve biomarker accessibility, we investigated two reagent-free electric-field (EF) strategies: post-capture EV permeabilization and direct high-frequency (HF) EF treatment of serum. Direct HF EF treatment temporarily permeabilized EV membranes, quickly transporting biomarkers to the sensor, enhancing target capture and nf-EIS response. Compared to EV isolation, serum HF EF treatment reduced assay time to 45 min and improved biomarker recovery. The platform achieved limit of detection ranging from 0.02 to 0.57 pg/mL for five clinically relevant EV biomarkers (TSG101, GM2AP, MUC1, MUC5AC, and EGFR). Clinical evaluation of serum samples from healthy subjects (n = 20) and lung cancer patients (n = 20) showed improved sensing performance, increasing ROC-AUC values from 0.870-0.984 to 0.985-1.000 and sensitivity by up to 16.7% following HF EF-treatment. These findings demonstrate that integrating BP-enabled signal amplification with EF-assisted EV biomarker release provides a rapid, reagent-free, and isolation-free nf-EIS platform for sensitive, multiplexed liquid biopsy, with potential for early cancer detection and decentralized clinical diagnostics.

records.title: Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms (PanNENs): From Historical Evolution to Precision Oncology in the Era of Molecular Imaging, Genomics, and Theranostics.
records.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PanNENs) are biologically heterogeneous tumors requiring individualized management based on grade, stage, functional status, and tumor biology. Advances in molecular classification, somatostatin receptor imaging, genomics, and theranostics have expanded precision management. Surgery, active surveillance, somatostatin analogs, targeted therapies, CAPTEM, peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, and liver-directed treatments now provide complementary options. Artificial intelligence, radiomics, and liquid biopsy may further support risk stratification and longitudinal monitoring. PanNEN management is evolving toward integrated precision oncology combining clinicopathological, molecular, functional imaging, and patient-specific information. Emerging technologies remain investigational and require prospective clinical validation.

records.title: Design, Synthesis, and Preclinical Evaluation of [18F]FPON, a First-In-Class PET Tracer Targeting Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen for Glioblastoma Imaging.
records.abstract: Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) is a central regulator of glioma stem cell maintenance and therapy resistance, yet no noninvasive method exists to visualize its expression in vivo. We developed [18F]FPON, a first-in-class small-molecule PET tracer targeting PCNA, derived from the clinical inhibitor AOH1996. FPON binds recombinant PCNA with a Kd of 900.8 ± 131.2 nM, comparable to AOH1996. [18F]FPON is synthesized in one step with a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 11.43 ± 4.03% (n = 6) and >95% radiochemical purity, readily crosses the blood-brain barrier, and remains >87% intact in brain at 60 min post-injection. In orthotopic U87 glioma xenografts, [18F]FPON exhibits specific tumor uptake (SUVr = 2.58 ± 0.38 vs contralateral brain), which is significantly reduced by AOH1996 (SUVr = 1.62 ± 0.24, p < 0.01). These results establish [18F]FPON as a promising PET tracer for noninvasive imaging of PCNA and support its potential use as a companion diagnostic for PCNA-targeted therapies.

records.title: Pancreatic cancer biomarkers and diagnostic tools (Review).
records.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by late presentation, early systemic dissemination and profound therapeutic resistance. Biomarkers are therefore required not only for early detection, but also for prognosis, treatment selection and longitudinal monitoring. The present review summarizes established and emerging PDAC biomarkers across genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and liquid biopsy. Particular attention is given to predictive biomarkers for personalized systemic therapy, including homologous-recombination repair defects associated with platinum sensitivity and eligibility for maintenance olaparib, as well as investigational markers of response to gemcitabine, fluoropyrimidines, irinotecan and oxaliplatin. The evolving role of companion diagnostics for germline BRCA1/2 variants and tumor-agnostic alterations is also discussed. In addition, the present review discusses biomarkers associated with occult or distant metastasis, including circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, the SMAD4 status and multi-modal radiomic models. CA19-9 remains the most commonly used serum marker; however, it is unsuitable for population screening and cannot independently establish diagnosis or metastatic risk. The majority of multi-omics candidates remain at the discovery or retrospective-validation stage. Their clinical translation requires analytically standardized assays, prospective validation in defined clinical settings and evidence that biomarker-guided decisions improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Efficient Capture and Isolation of Extracellular Vesicles for Cancer Liquid Biopsy: Emerging Technologies and Clinical Perspectives.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), which carry diverse molecular components including proteins, RNA, DNA, lipids, and carbohydrates and are critically involved in cancer initiation and progression, are considered promising liquid biopsy biomarkers for early detection. However, clinical translation remains bottlenecked by the lack of isolation technologies that simultaneously achieve high purity, high yield, and rapid processing. While traditional methods have laid the foundation, their inherent trade-offs between purity, throughput, and scalability limit clinical utility. We survey recent progress across four major technology classes categorized by their working principles-membrane-lipid-targeting, affinity-based, microfluidic, and nanomaterial platforms-and evaluate their performance against clinical requirements. Unlike prior reviews that catalogue methods by physical principles alone, this review adopts a clinically oriented evaluation framework that assesses each technology against performance metrics demanded by distinct applications-early screening (high throughput), therapeutic monitoring (high purity/reproducibility), and multi-marker prognosis (multiplexing). Finally, we discuss key challenges such as nonspecific adsorption control, multi-marker co-capture. This review provides a comparative reference to facilitate technology selection for specific diagnostic or therapeutic needs, thereby supporting the broader adoption of liquid biopsy in precision oncology.

records.title: Dynamic changes in cytokine levels as potential prognostic biomarkers in cancer immunotherapy.
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have reshaped cancer therapy, yet fewer than 20% of patients achieve durable benefit and many develop immune-related adverse events, highlighting the need for accessible biomarkers to support treatment decisions. Circulating cytokines obtained through liquid biopsy offer a minimally invasive means to monitor systemic immune activity and represent exploratory, hypothesis-generating indicators of immune modulation during ICI therapy. We retrospectively analyzed clinical data and paired plasma samples from patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors treated within early-phase ICI-based trials at IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital (2019-2023). Blood was collected at baseline and at first radiologic assessment. Thirteen cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-8, CXCL10, CCL2, TGF-β1) were quantified using a multiplex bead-based assay, and longitudinal changes were classified as positive, negative, or null. Exploratory associations with disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS), and treatment duration were evaluated. Immunohistochemistry for CD3, CD68, and CD66b was performed to explore descriptive correlations between cytokine modulation and tumor immune contexture. Sixty-six patients were included. Positive IL-1β variation was associated with higher DCR (p=0.022). OS showed exploratory associations with positive changes in IL-1β, IL-12p70, and IL-4. Concordant cytokine modulation across these cytokines was frequent (all p<0.001). Increased IFN-γ correlated with longer treatment duration. Patients with at least one positive cytokine change displayed higher CD3+ T-cell density and lower CD66b+ neutrophil infiltration. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that paired longitudinal cytokine profiling may complement tissue-based biomarkers and inform future personalized immunotherapy strategies.
